title: The world’s largest mud building gets a fresh coat of mud every year
body: The Great Mosque of Djenné, in Mali, is the largest adobe building in the world. A mosque has stood on the site since around the 13th century, but the present one was finished in 1907. Its walls of sun-baked earth bricks rise from a platform about 75 metres square, with a central tower around 16 metres high. Every year the rains eat into the walls, so at an annual festival the **whole town turns out to replaster them**, climbing the palm sticks that bristle from the walls: the toron are decoration and ready-made scaffolding in one.

slides.label: each side of the raised platform the mosque stands on
slides.text: The platform is 3 metres above the level of the marketplace, and the central tower rises about 16 metres.

slides.heading: The Great Mosque in metres
slides.note: The tower’s height is approximate; the platform lifts the mosque 3 m above the marketplace.

slides.heading: The yearly repair
items: Rain erodes the walls; heat and humidity open cracks
At the festival, the whole community turns out to plaster
Workers climb the toron, palm sticks jutting 60 cm from the walls

events.text: A first mosque is built on the site
UNESCO lists it with the Old Towns of Djenné
Part of a tower collapses after 75 mm of rain in a day

slides.heading: Built from the ground it stands on
slides.text: The bricks, called ferey, are sun-baked earth, set in a mortar of sand and earth. A building like this survives only because people keep renewing it, and the town has turned that renewal into a celebration.

slides.question: Why does the mosque need replastering every year?
slides.explanation: Mostly erosion from the annual rains, plus cracks from changes in temperature and humidity. In 2009 part of a tower collapsed after 75 mm of rain fell in 24 hours.

slides.clue: The palm sticks bristling from the walls: decoration, and scaffolding for the yearly replastering
slides.detail: Bundles of palm sticks built into the walls; they jut out about 60 cm and carry the plasterers each year.
